findings.problem: signal is "silent", but the evidence shows 0.19.0 `createMcpHandler` took an SDK v1 `McpServer | Server` instance while 0.20.0 requires a v2 `McpServerFactory`, so old code that passes a v1 server (or a v1 factory function, which is now always treated as v2) no longer type-checks or works; mark it loud, or prove with a runtime test that the old call still succeeds.

The sentence tells an assistant that code written for older versions still runs unchanged, which would lead it to keep passing SDK v1 servers to `createMcpHandler` instead of switching to `createLegacyMcpHandler` or a v2 factory; rewrite the claim to say v1 servers must move to `createLegacyMcpHandler`.

The claim asserts runtime behavior (function inputs are always treated as v2 factories, and concurrent Worker requests get isolated server instances), but the tests only regex-scan `.d.ts` type declarations and never call the handler; narrow the claim to the signature change, or add a runtime test that shows per-request isolation.

The entry and the test both name `createLegacyMcpHandler` as the path for SDK v1 servers, but the lesson has no replacement field, and kind "behavior" hides that the accepted parameter type changed; add replacement `createLegacyMcpHandler` and use a kind that reflects the signature change.

The lesson mixes a loud part (passing a v1 server instance to `createMcpHandler` no longer works) with a silent-sounding part (function inputs are now treated as v2 factories that isolate requests); split them into separate lessons.

The claim says the client falls back to the legacy initialize handshake on the same connection, but the tests only grep source for a v2 Client import and a server/discover string, so nothing checks the fallback; either add a test that connects to a legacy server and sees initialize sent on the same connection, or drop the fallback part of the claim.

Both runs are static source greps, and the pass condition reads the hoisted @modelcontextprotocol/client that the test pinned itself, not the copy agents actually loads; the old run fails on 'uses the SDK v1 Client', an import-path proxy, rather than on the change's own symptom (no server/discover request sent), so use a pair that connects MCPClientConnection to a mock server and checks whether server/discover is received.

The claim says the PartyServer runtime is vendored into `agents/lifecycle`, but the tests only grep the base class of `Agent` in dist and never check that `agents/lifecycle` exists or exports anything; drop that clause or add a test that imports `agents/lifecycle`.

The lesson is marked silent, but neither test runs code written for 0.21.0 on 0.22.0. Both only regex-match source text, so nothing shows that code depending on the old `Server` base (for example `instanceof Server` or partyserver-only members) still runs without error; add a test that runs old-style Agent code on 0.22.0, or leave the signal unclaimed.

The sentence says the change alters what `Agent` does and that old code still runs, but the evidence only shows a changed superclass in the bundled source, which an assistant could misread as a guarantee of runtime compatibility; limit the claim to the inheritance change the tests prove.

The detail says hasSubAgent(), listSubAgents(), abortSubAgent() and deleteSubAgent() are deprecated from 0.23.0, but the tests only check the @deprecated tag on subAgent(), and the quote comes from the 0.27.0 docs, so the siblings' deprecation is unproven at the start of the range; either test each sibling's @deprecated tag in 0.23.0 or limit the detail to subAgent().

The lesson has no tests, so nothing shows a queued callback seeing `connection`/`request` via getCurrentAgent() on the release before 0.24.0 and losing them on 0.24.0. Add a differential pair where the old run fails only on that missing-connection symptom and any other failure prints ERROR.

`versions` is ">=0.24.0", but the only evidence is a quote from the CHANGELOG pinned at agents@0.27.0, and the quoted text names no release. Cite the 0.24.0 changelog section or confirm the starting release with tests, then correct `versions` if it differs.

The quote names `useAgent` and the two wire values but never names the `transport` option the lesson is about, and it is cut off mid-sentence ("through a single"); quote the docs passage that shows the `transport` option itself, e.g. `transport: "capnweb"` on `useAgent`/`AgentClient`, as a complete sentence.

The detail says inline projects inherit options from the root config in general, but the tests only show that root `setupFiles` is inherited; either narrow the claim to what was tested (e.g. 'such as setupFiles') or add tests covering other root options.

The detail says the matcher checks that text is "exactly equal" to the expected string, but the tests only show that a substring ('Error' against 'Error!') no longer matches; they never check whitespace normalization, RegExp arguments, or options. Narrow the claim to "a substring of the text no longer matches", or add tests that cover whitespace and RegExp inputs.

The detail says Vitest stores "all blob test results" in .vitest/blob/, but the tests cover only one unsharded run with no outputFile set; drop "all" and say the default report path moved from .vitest-reports/ to .vitest/blob/ unless --outputFile is set.

The symbol is only `--merge-reports`, but the entry and the quote describe the blob reporter's default output folder, and the old run fails on the blob reporter's write path; name the blob reporter output (outputFile) as the symbol, or name both, so the symbol matches the change the tests show.

The claim says `--repeats` repeats "every test," but the primary source says a test's own `repeats` option takes precedence over the CLI value, and the tests never cover that case; the claim should be limited to tests without their own `repeats` option.

An assistant reading "repeats every test regardless of the result" could expect `--repeats N` to override a per-test `{ repeats }` option and write wrong code; the sentence should say that a per-test `repeats` option takes precedence over the CLI value.

The quoted source is the blog announcement ("which is useful for hunting flaky tests") rather than the primary-source sentence, so it leaves out the precedence rule; quote the primary source, including the sentence on per-test `repeats` precedence.

The quote is a migration-guide how-to with garbled example text ('bash $ cd subdir && vitest $ cd subdir && vitest --config …') that never names `vitest.config` or states the lookup rule; quote the primary-source sentence instead: "Vitest looks for vitest.config.{ts,…} first and vite.config.{ts,…} second in the project root. If no config file is found, Vitest will run without one."

The replacement in `detail` gives only `--config`, but the quoted source says to pass the config explicitly and also scope test discovery with `--dir`; add `--dir` so the replacement matches the source.

Following the advice to pass only `--config ../vitest.config.ts` from a subdirectory would likely make the parent the root and run the whole parent project's tests, and the rendered 'changed what `vitest.config` does' wrongly implies the config file's meaning changed rather than where Vitest looks for it; reword to say Vitest 5 only looks for the config in the project root and no longer in parent directories, and give `--config <path> --dir .` as the fix.

The detail says the Vite plugin also rewrites the old path, but the tests only inspect wrangler's ProxyWorker.js and bundled miniflare, never @cloudflare/vite-plugin; drop the Vite plugin claim or add a test that covers it.
The detail says 'the old paths' rewrite to 'the new ones', which reads as every `/cdn-cgi/*` path, but the tests check only `/cdn-cgi/handler/scheduled`; narrow the wording to that one path.

The claim covers `--latest` on every command, but the tests only exercise `wrangler deploy --dry-run --latest` and the entry names only `deploy` and `versions upload`; scope the claim to `wrangler deploy --latest`, or add a `versions upload` test before naming both.

The quote is the flag's help text, which repeats the changelog headline ('Use the latest compatibility date supported by this version of Wrangler') and never states the fact the tests check, that the date is the bundled workerd's release date; quote a source that states that.
The symbol `--latest` is a bare flag that matches flags on unrelated commands; it should name the command, e.g. `wrangler deploy --latest`.

The sentence only restates the help text and says nothing about the old or new value, so an assistant would not learn that `--latest` now pins the bundled workerd's release date instead of the newest runtime, and that compatibility flags dated after that release are not enabled; state the old and new resolved date explicitly.

The claim says connect entries deliver raw socket connections to the connect(socket, env, ctx) handler during wrangler dev, but the tests only run `deploy --dry-run` and check that the config field is accepted and its port validated; either narrow the claim to config acceptance and validation, or add a test that starts wrangler dev and opens a TCP connection to the handler.

The claim leaves out that the feature is experimental and local-only (deployed Workers cannot yet accept inbound sockets), so an assistant could add a connect entry expecting production Workers to receive TCP connections; state the local-dev-only, experimental limitation in the detail.

The lesson is marked loud, but the tests delete CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN; the quote says the CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN fallback remains, so a project that sets both variables (common in CI) has WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN ignored with no error. Either add a test that shows this case also fails, or say in the claim that the failure is only loud when CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN is not set.

The claim says null values delete secrets, but both tests only grep the `--help` text for a documentation sentence and never run a deletion; add a test that runs `versions secret bulk` with a null-valued key against a mocked API and checks that a delete is issued, or narrow the claim to what is tested.

The pair separates 4.147.0 from 4.148.0 only by help wording, not by the change's own symptom (null deleting a secret instead of being rejected or stored), so the old run's FAIL does not show the behavior is missing; rewrite both tests to exercise a null key and assert the deletion outcome.

Code that never sets a value to null behaves the same on 4.148.0, so null-as-delete is new opt-in capability; kind should be `added`, not `behavior`, and the generated sentence should not say the command 'changed what it does'.

The detail says the previous command paths still work as hidden aliases, but no test runs `wrangler r2 sql` on 4.145.0; add a test that the old path still succeeds on the new version, or drop the alias claim.
The quote never names the new symbol `wrangler basin sql` and only describes the commands as stable aliases; quote the sentence that says R2 SQL now lives under `wrangler basin sql`.

Signal is silent, but the same entry says `WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` is no longer read, so old code that authenticates with it now fails; the silent claim is unsupported unless the token change is split out and the alias is tested.

The entry has a loud part (the `WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` to `WRANGLER_BASIN_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` switch) next to the silent command rename; put the token change in its own lesson with loud signal and its own tests.

The quote comes from the 4.148.0 changelog and says the commands are 'now stable' with hidden aliases, but versions starts at 4.145.0 based only on `basin` existing there; confirm which release added the aliases and cite that release's entry, or align versions with it.

'Code written for older versions still runs, without an error' would lead an assistant to keep setting `WRANGLER_R2_SQL_AUTH_TOKEN` for `wrangler r2 sql`, which no longer authenticates; the sentence must not promise unchanged behavior while the token variable changed.

The quote only explains how to turn Node.js compatibility off with `no_nodejs_compat` and `no_nodejs_compat_v2`; it never says that `nodejs_compat` is on by default from 2026-08-04 or names `nodejs_compat`, so it does not state the default change the lesson claims. Fix: cite a source sentence that states the new default and names `nodejs_compat`.

The claim says Node.js compatibility as a whole is on, but the tests only show that a `dry-run` build resolves a bare `path` import; they never check runtime Node.js APIs or the effect of removing positive flags. Fix: narrow the detail to what was tested, or add tests that cover runtime behavior.

The detail says telemetry is disabled 'regardless of other telemetry settings', but both tests only override the WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS env var; other settings such as `wrangler telemetry enable` or the config's send_metrics are never tested. Narrow the claim to WRANGLER_SEND_METRICS, or add tests for the other settings.

The claim says the strategy defaults to deferred with a 5-minute delay whenever it is unset, but the evidence covers only `wrangler deploy` of a new Worker (the changelog likewise says "Deploys"), so the detail should say this applies to `wrangler deploy` rather than implying every command or upload path.
